summary.intent: Bootstrap release-please with proper version tags after phase 41 setup, align api-client versions with the API, and implement a new feature exposing API version on the /health endpoint — while iteratively fixing the CI release preview workflow.
summary.outcome: Successfully bootstrapped 15 release-please tags, aligned api-client versions to 0.35.0, added version to /health endpoint with shared version module, and significantly improved the PR release preview workflow to write release-as targets directly to the PR branch (eliminating the post-merge push-to-main approach that failed due to branch protection).

repo: release-please treats entire commit history as unreleased when no prior tags exist — bootstrap tags must be created at the pre-history SHA to get clean changelogs
The health endpoint spec is manually defined in generate-openapi.ts (not via NestJS decorators) because HealthController depends on TypeOrmHealthIndicator which requires a real DB connection
Phase 41 discussion log (41-DISCUSSION-LOG.md:106) explicitly decided monotonic versioning for web/desktop, but semver was implemented — decision was consciously deferred
The project uses conventional commits for release-please bump computation; commit type (feat/fix/chore) directly determines which packages get version bumps
pnpm api:generate regenerates openapi.json via ts-node generate-openapi.ts, then runs orval to generate the typed client, then builds with tsup
GitHub Actions push tokens do not trigger new workflow runs (recursion prevention) — useful for the PR branch commit-back approach
Legacy branch protection rules lack per-actor bypass support; only rulesets support that feature

code.finding: HealthController is excluded from the NestJS OpenAPI generator module; health endpoint schema is manually defined further down in the script
API version reading was refactored to use a shared src/version.ts module instead of inline process.env.npm_package_version with fallback to reading package.json
Merge commits (2+ parents) must be filtered before conventional commit parsing — without this, merge commits trigger false bump labels across all packages
Manual label overrides must be fed back into packageBumps map; otherwise release-as derivation uses the computed (lower) bump instead of the manual (higher) label
Contains 15 package version entries; crates/api-client was at 0.4.0 and packages/api-client at 0.33.0 — both misaligned with apps/api at 0.35.0

workflow: release-please bootstrap: create tags at the last-known-good SHA using manifest versions, push them, then re-run the workflow — no config changes needed
Using chore(ci): commit prefix instead of fix: prevents release-please from triggering unwanted patch version bumps
The post-merge push-to-main CI pattern is fundamentally incompatible with branch protection requiring status checks — prefer writing config changes to the PR branch before merge
Squashing multiple commits into one chore(ci): requires soft reset to the branch divergence point, restaging all changes, and force pushing
npm_package_version env var is unreliable in all contexts; always fall back to reading package.json from disk
When resolving PR review threads: reply via REST API using --field for integer in_reply_to, then resolve via GraphQL mutation

friction: cargo update pulled in unrelated dependency churn when updating crate version — required manually patching only the workspace crate entries in Cargo.lock
git index.lock file left by a background agent prevented switching branches
post-merge-release workflow failed because GitHub App token cannot bypass branch protection required status checks — required significant redesign
Legacy branch protection UI lacks per-actor bypass (only rulesets support it), discovered only after attempting option 1
release-please workflow showed incomplete changelog on PR #430 because post-merge job never ran — appeared like a bug but was actually expected given the job failure
Background agent task failure notification appeared after the fix was already committed manually — caused confusion
auto-merge was reported as enabled by user but gh pr view showed autoMergeRequest: null — required manual merge
open_items: release:none early-return now clears stale release-as entries but must compare against base branch config to avoid clearing entries set by previously merged PRs — partial fix applied, thread 1 of final review round

bump-minor-pre-major: true is set on all packages in release-please-config.json but the version computation in pr-release-preview.js doesn't account for it — would produce 1.0.0 on breaking change instead of 0.x+1.0
Monotonic versioning for web and desktop apps was the original design intent (per 41-DISCUSSION-LOG.md) but semver is in use — consciously deferred
PR #430 (release PR) changelog may still be incomplete if post-release targets were never applied — needs verification after PR #431 merges and release-please re-runs
The release preview workflow self-test on PR #431 should confirm the commit-back approach works end-to-end
